# Check of M0-x-04: the base registration table and §4.1's order assertion over the whole M0 stage set (lane `check/M0-x-04`, flow flow-7, stage group 15, 2026-10-07)

Lane `check/M0-x-04` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows PC (WSL2, Linux x64, Node 24.12.0).
`tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:16gib`. The seat ran on
2026-10-07 from about 15:24 to 17:00. It is an implementer-side independent checker and not the item's author (the
author's lane is `build/M0-x-04`, ledger rows L-0325 and L-0328). This is the full first check of M0-x-04. It is not a
re-check.

The seat ran no git command and changed no file of the item. It planned its probes and mutants before it read the
author's self-check lines. It ran one vitest process of its own at a time, except for the mutant sweep (three mirrors,
`--maxWorkers=1` each, `test_budget.py --mutants` = 3) and two paired probe runs (two mirrors, one worker each). Worker
counts came from `tools/test_budget.py` (8 in this window). Its mirrors are
`~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-x-04/m1` to `m3`. Each mirror is an rsync copy of `plat/` without `node_modules`,
installed with `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` (exit 0). In each mirror, 0 symbolic links resolve
outside the mirror. The mirrors' `node_modules` were deleted at the end. The logs, the probe files and `mutants.py` are
in that folder. The checker's ledger row is **L-0329**.

## Verdict: FAIL — one blocker

The registration table, the order, the op forms, the two listed tests and the here-bar all hold, and 38 of 42 targeted
mutants were killed. One composition contract fails on an honest input. The base's S6 adapter gives S6 the bridges S1
laid (all of them in state `site`) instead of the bridges S4 built. As a result, a bridge that S4 builds never seeds
§4.5's bridgehead wards. On `RIVER_BLUEPRINT` at seed 5 (the test frame of 900 ha, 30 ha walled), S4 builds
`bridge:8` on the `through` way `way:5`. The districts S6 writes then differ from the districts S6 writes when it is
given S4's bridges (details under B1).

| # | blocker | evidence | required change | label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B1** | `base.ts:631` (`baseS6Input`): `siteFeatures(p, { …, bridges: input.water.bridges, … })` passes S1's water record's bridges to S6's sited features. S1 lays crossing **sites** only. S4 returns its built bridges as new objects (`backbone/commit.ts:602` `{ ...b, state: 'built', way: w }`) under the data key `bridges`. S6's item declares that key as an input (`districts/stage.ts:487` `inputs: ['ways', 'gates', 'bridges', …]`), and the base's S6 adapter inherits the declaration through `strs(item.inputs, …)`, but its `inputsOf` never reads the key. `siteFeatures` keeps only bridges with `b.state === 'built'` (`districts/stage.ts:205`), so under `runBase` no bridgehead feature is ever sited, whatever S4 builds. This is a silently wrong result on an honest input and an interface that disagrees with the item it hands to (S4 → S6, and the harnesses M0-e-06 and M0-c-06 that call `runBase`; §1 (e)'s bar "gate / bridgehead wards' median area" reads these wards). C-0264 (5) wrote "S1's water and bridges", which reads as S1's records. | **Probe 4** (m1, S1–S5 registered, 900 ha, 24 runs: rivers from 0 / 9 000 / 18 000 / 27 000 cdeg × seeds 1–6): S4 built a bridge on 3 runs: `{"bearing":27000,"seed":5,"bugs":[],"s4built":[["bridge:8","way:5"]],"s1states":["site", … (18 × "site")]}`, also bearing 27 000 seed 2 and bearing 0 seed 5 (where S5 refuses later). **Probe 5** (RIVER_BLUEPRINT, seed 5, full base run; m1 = the tree's `base.ts`, m2 = the same file with S6 given the data key `bridges` and falling back to `water.bridges`; diff in `fed-patch.diff`): `base n 17 dh fa4f523d9e2b0b22 lanes 164 root [2824633860,987442918,4213800740,3173947472] seeds 7 leftovers 10` against `fed n 17 dh e06c0e81634fdd9f lanes 170 root [3079720843,854149411,1747351769,1811385130] seeds 9 leftovers 8`. The way is `way5: ["through"]`. Both runs have `bugs []`. The two extra seeds are the deck ends of `bridge:8`. **Mutant M52** (`bridges: []` in the same call) survived the item's whole test set. Probe 3 showed why: on the tested fixtures (river W seeds 1 and 3, river N seed 2) S4 builds no bridge, so S1's bridges and `[]` give the same S6 (`built: []`, identical roots). No test exercises a built bridge reaching S6. | In `base.ts`'s S6 adapter, read the declared data key `bridges` (S4's output) in `inputsOf`, and pass those bridges to `siteFeatures`. Fall back to `water.bridges` only when the key is absent. Check that no other S6 or fields input takes a bridge's state from S1's record. Add a `run.test.ts` case on a fixture where S4 builds a bridge (for example `RIVER` at seed 5 on the 900 ha frame, which has `bugs []`). It must assert that the built bridge reaches S6: S6's sited features hold `bridge:8/end:0` and `/end:1` (or the report's `seeds` counts them), and the result must differ from a run that withholds S4's bridges. That test must kill mutant M52. Append a choices row that refines C-0264 (5): S6's bridges are S4's. | CONFIRMED |

The verdict rests only on B1. Every other finding below is MINOR and goes to `checks/M0-x-04-notes.md` for the
hardening milestone M4.

### The seat's own probes (mirror m1, never the tree)

- **Probe 1 (fail-safety, order, façade completeness), 18 runs**: flat, river W and river N × seeds 1–6, 900 ha,
  30 ha walled. The mirror's runner was instrumented to count every `onCommit`. Results: **no run threw**. The order
  is `S1S3S4S5S6S8` in every run. The number of commits equals the batches the façade watch saw committed in every
  run (for example flat 1: `commits 22 obs 22`). The forms are always a subset of
  `S1:callback, S3:declared, S4:declared, S5a:callback, S5b:declared, S5c:callback, S6:callback, S8:callback`. S8
  refused no district. Four runs end with an S5 refusal recorded as the run's one bug, as C-0264 (13) lists:
  river W 2 `E_DEGENERATE`, river N 1 and 6 `E_SELF_INTERSECT`, river N 5 `E_INVARIANT`. Their details (probe 2) are
  `F-WALL: the trace touches itself after the re-offset and union-simplify rungs; the later rungs are M1's`,
  `E_DEGENERATE stretch` and `trace: gate gate:5 is not on the committed trace at its point`. These come from
  M0-c-04's trace code at a river. They fail safe (see note 1). CONFIRMED.
- **Probe 1b (determinism across processes)**: six of the runs (flat, river W and river N at seeds 1 and 2) were
  repeated in a second vitest process. Every root and every recorded field was equal (`root equal across processes:
  True`, `all fields equal: True` ×6). CONFIRMED.
- **Probe 3**: S6's districts, typing, quarters and seams, and the root, for river W 1, river W 3 and river N 2, with
  the tree's `base.ts`, with mutant M51, and with mutant M52. All three variants gave identical hashes and roots, and
  no built bridge appeared (`built: []`). Probes 4 and 5 followed from this (B1).
- **Probes 4 and 5**: see B1.
